name: Taco Bundt Cake
desc: Seasoned beef, cheese, pico and crushed Doritos baked inside a ring of flour tortillas in a bundt pan, then flipped out and sliced.

source.title: Taco Bundt Cake
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 2 cups Nacho Cheese Doritos, lightly crushed

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Coat a 10- to 12-cup bundt pan generously with cooking spray.
Brown the beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains (160°F), 6-8 minutes. Drain the fat.
Stir in the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, taco seasoning and water. Simmer until the liquid is absorbed and the meat is saucy, 3-5 minutes. Let it cool a few minutes.
Cut 6 tortillas in half. Line the pan with the halves, cut edge against the center tube and rounded edge draping over the outer rim, overlapping so no pan shows.
Sprinkle 1 cup of cheese over the tortillas. Add half the beef, half the pico and half the crushed Doritos.
Repeat with another 1 cup of cheese, the rest of the beef, pico and Doritos, and finish with the last 1 cup of cheese.
Fold the overhanging tortilla over the filling. Cut the remaining 2 tortillas into strips and patch any gaps, then press down firmly to seal.
Bake until the top is golden and crisp, 40-45 minutes.
Cool in the pan for 20 minutes so the cheese sets. Set a serving plate on top, flip, and lift off the pan.
Slice and serve with sour cream and shredded lettuce.
tips: Drain the pico well or the bottom layer steams instead of crisping.
Tasty's version (Crunchy Taco Ring) bakes at 350°F for 45 minutes and rests 20 minutes before flipping; the rest is what lets it hold its shape.

references.title: Crunchy Taco Ring
